generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A workflow can look correct on its happy path while a secondary persisted horizon overrides canonical state, asynchronous processing substitutes worker time for event time, or cleanup removes the durable reference required after a partial failure.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: A developer reuses convenient persisted timestamps and best-effort cleanup ordering without adversarially separating canonical versus derived time sources or failing between authoritative and secondary effects.

reusable_control.rule: Use deliberately divergent time sources and fail between durable primary state and secondary effects; require canonical time and a restart-safe repair source.

generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Before implementation, identify the canonical horizon and event-time source for every business window and preserve a durable repair reference until every mandatory secondary effect is idempotently resolved.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Audit with conflicting canonical/denormalized horizons, delayed event processing, and an injected failure between primary commit and secondary effect followed by a fresh repair cycle.

transfer_cases.case: A cached expiry is shorter than a canonical grace deadline; the canonical deadline must govern.
Primary revocation commits, secondary notification fails, and a fresh worker reconstructs the missing effect without memory.
A persisted event is processed late; its business window remains anchored to event time.
